extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent applicants (including pro se), patent practitioners, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory requirements for preparing and arranging the specification, abstract, drawings, detailed description, claims, and related parts of a U.S. utility patent application in compliance with the MPEP and 37 CFR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement of the Sections of the Specification
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification of a utility application should include the listed sections in order (a) TITLE OF THE INVENTION; (b) CROSS-REFERENCE TO RELATED APPLICATIONS; (c) STATEMENT REGARDING FEDERALLY SPONSORED RESEARCH OR DEVELOPMENT; (d) THE NAMES OF THE PARTIES TO A JOINT RESEARCH AGREEMENT; (e) INCORPORATION-BY-REFERENCE OF MATERIAL SUBMITTED ON A COMPACT DISC OR AS A TEXT FILE VIA EFS-WEB; (f) STATEMENT REGARDING PRIOR DISCLOSURES BY THE INVENTOR OR A JOINT INVENTOR; (g) BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION; (h) BRIEF SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION; (i) BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE SEVERAL VIEWS OF THE DRAWING(S); (j) DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION; (k) CLAIM OR CLAIMS (commencing on a separate sheet); (l) ABSTRACT OF THE DISCLOSURE (commencing on a separate sheet); (m) SEQUENCE LISTING.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each lettered item should appear in upper case as a section heading; if no text follows a heading, state 'Not Applicable'. See 37 CFR 1.77(b). Claims and abstract must commence on separate sheets. See MPEP cross-references for design, plant, and reissue applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title of the Invention (placement and content)
rubrics_metrics.description: The title should be placed at the top of the first page of the specification unless provided in an application data sheet. The title should be brief but technically accurate and descriptive, preferably from two to seven words, and may not contain more than 500 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.72(a) and MPEP § 606. Avoid repeating title information in the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-References to Related Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Include cross-references to related applications in the specification where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow 37 CFR 1.78 and MPEP § 211 et seq. Use the appropriate section heading in the ordered specification layout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement Regarding Federally Sponsored Research or Development
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a statement if the invention was made under federally sponsored research or development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 310 for required content and form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Names of Parties to a Joint Research Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification should include the names of the parties to a joint research agreement when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.71(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation-by-Reference of Electronic Material
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification is required to include an incorporation-by-reference of electronic documents that are to become part of the permanent USPTO records (e.g., material submitted on a compact disc or as a text file via EFS-Web).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.52(e), MPEP § 608.05, MPEP § 502.05 and the USPTO Legal Framework for EFS-Web.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement Regarding Prior Disclosures by Inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a statement regarding prior disclosures by the inventor or joint inventor as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 35 U.S.C. 102(b) and 37 CFR 1.77.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background of the Invention (field and related art)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Background should set forth: (1) Field of the Invention — a statement of the field of art to which the invention pertains (may paraphrase applicable U.S. patent classification); (2) Description of the Related Art — description of related art known to applicant, including references and problems in the prior art solved by the invention, and information disclosed under 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement should be directed to the subject matter of the claimed invention. See MPEP § 608.01(c) and related cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief Summary of the Invention (content and purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief summary or general statement of the invention directed to the invention (not the disclosure as a whole) that may point out advantages or how it solves prior art problems; the nature and gist of the inventive concept should be set forth where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should be commensurate with the invention as claimed and consistent with the claims. Objects of the invention may be stated briefly only to the extent they aid understanding. See 37 CFR 1.73 and MPEP § 608.01(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief Description of the Several Views of the Drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: When there are drawings, include a brief description of the several views and refer to different views by figure numbers in the detailed description; parts should be identified by reference letters or numerals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.74 and MPEP § 608.01(f). Examiner should ensure all figures described are present and correctly referred to; object if description refers to figures not present (e.g., refers only to Figure 1 when Figures 1A, 1B, 1C exist).

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed Description of the Invention (enablement and sufficiency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe preferred embodiment(s) required by 37 CFR 1.71 in such particularity as to enable a person skilled in the art to make and use the invention without undue experimentation and to clearly convey enough information to show that applicant invented the claimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Description should be as short and specific as necessary. Conventional elements need not be described in detail unless not widely known. Where complexity warrants, refer to another patent or readily available publication. Reference characters must be properly applied (no single character used for two different parts). The description serves as a dictionary for the claims and must provide clear support or antecedent basis for all claim terms. See MPEP § 608.01(g) and cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference Characters and Illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference characters must be properly applied; no single reference character may be used for two different parts or for a part and a modification of that part. Every feature specified in the claims must be illustrated, but there should be no superfluous illustrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.84(p) and MPEP guidance cited in the detailed description and drawing sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Mode Requirement (mode of operation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The best mode contemplated by the inventor for carrying out the invention must be set forth in the description (35 U.S.C. 112).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No statutory requirement for disclosure of a specific example; absence or presence of a working example is not dispositive of best mode. Only evidence of concealment tends to show inadequate best mode disclosure. Failure to disclose the best mode at filing cannot be cured by post-filing amendment; such an amendment should be treated as new matter. See MPEP § 608.01(h) and related case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims: Statutory Requirement and Structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must conclude with claims 'particularly pointing out and distinctly claiming' the subject matter inventor regards as the invention (35 U.S.C. 112). Claims must conform to the invention as set forth in the specification and claim terms must find clear support or antecedent basis in the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More than one claim permitted if they differ substantially and are not unduly multiplied. Dependent claims are permitted and must refer back; multiple dependent claims have special rules (refer only in the alternative, cannot be basis for another multiple dependent claim). For fee purposes, multiple dependent and dependent-from-multiple-dependent claims are treated by number of references. See 37 CFR 1.75 and MPEP § 608.01(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims: Form and Ordering for Improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable (e.g., improvement claims), an independent claim should contain in the following order: (1) a preamble comprising a general description of all elements/steps that are conventional or known; (2) a phrase such as 'wherein the improvement comprises'; (3) those elements/steps/relationships considered new or improved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested order to clarify which portions are known and which are claimed as improvement. See MPEP § 608.01(i)(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims: Commencement, Indentation and Separation
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must commence on a separate physical sheet or electronic page; where a claim sets forth a plurality of elements or steps, each element or step should be separated by a line indentation. There may be plural indentations to further segregate subcombinations or related steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Original numbering of claims must be preserved throughout prosecution. When claims are canceled, remaining claims must not be renumbered. When claims are added, they must be numbered by the applicant consecutively beginning with the number next following the highest numbered claim previously presented (whether entered or not).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When application is ready for allowance the examiner may renumber claims consecutively in the order they appear or as requested by applicant. In a single claim case, the claim is not numbered. See 37 CFR 1.126 and MPEP § 608.01(j).

rubrics_metrics.name: Least Restrictive Claim as Claim 1 and Grouping of Dependent Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The least restrictive claim should be presented as claim number 1, and all dependent claims should be grouped together with the claim(s) to which they refer to the extent practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitates examination and clarity. See MPEP § 608.01(i)(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract of the Disclosure: Placement and Basic Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief abstract of the technical disclosure must commence on a separate sheet, preferably following the claims, under the heading 'Abstract' or 'Abstract of the Disclosure.' The sheet(s) presenting the abstract may not include other parts or material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPAP will review compliance and require an abstract if none filed. Examiners should point out defects in the first Office action or at earliest point and require compliance (use form paragraphs as applicable). See 37 CFR 1.72(b) and MPEP § 608.01(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract of the Disclosure: Content (what to include and avoid)
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract should be a concise statement of the technical disclosure and should include that which is new in the art to which the invention pertains. It should not refer to purported merits or speculative applications and should not compare the invention with prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If basic in nature, abstract may be directed to entire disclosure; if an improvement, include technical disclosure of the improvement. Where applicable, include: organization/operation (machine), method of making (article), identity/use (chemical compound), ingredients (mixture), steps (process). Avoid extensive mechanical/design details. For chemical patents, give general nature and use; for processes, state type of reaction, reagents and process conditions, generally illustrated by a single example. See MPEP § 608.01(b)(B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract of the Disclosure: Language and Format
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract should be in narrative form and generally limited to a single paragraph preferably within the range of 50 to 150 words (preferably not exceeding 150 words). The abstract should not exceed 15 lines of text. Avoid claim legal phraseology (e.g., 'means', 'said') and avoid repeating information given in the title or using phrases that can be implied (e.g., 'This disclosure concerns').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 6.16.01 may be used if the abstract does not commence on a separate sheet. Examiners should check overlength abstracts for conciseness. Abstract is part of the specification for purposes of 35 U.S.C. 112 (In re Armbruster). See MPEP § 608.01(b)(C)-(D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract: Examiner and Applicant Responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation of the abstract is the responsibility of the applicant; review of the abstract for compliance is the responsibility of the examiner. Any necessary amendment to the abstract at time of allowance or printer query must be made by applicant or examiner with applicant's approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replies requiring a new abstract or amendment to bring into compliance should be treated under 37 CFR 1.111(b) like any other formal matter and carefully reviewed for introduction of new matter (35 U.S.C. 132). Examiners generally should make necessary revisions by formal examiner's amendment after obtaining applicant's authorization rather than issuing an Ex parte Quayle action. See MPEP § 608.01(b)(D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract: Examiner Actions for Missing or Defective Abstracts
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application lacks an abstract or the abstract does not comply with guidelines, the examiner should require submission of a compliant abstract in the first Office action or at earliest point noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate form paragraphs (e.g., 6.12, 6.13, 6.14, 6.16) and consider national stage exceptions. For pro se applicants, follow specified form-paragraph sequences. See MPEP § 608.01(b) and related form paragraph notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings: Standards for Media, Color, and Photographs
rubrics_metrics.description: Black-and-white drawings (India ink or equivalent) are normally required. Color drawings are permitted in design applications and rarely in utility applications upon petition and meeting conditions. Photographs are not ordinarily permitted but are acceptable if they are the only practicable medium for illustrating the claimed invention; color photographs follow color drawing rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Color drawings in utility apps require a petition with fee, one set via EFS-Web or three sets otherwise, and insertion of prescribed language in the brief description of the drawings. Color must be reproducible in black-and-white in printed patent. Photographs must be of sufficient quality so that all details are reproducible in the printed patent. See 37 CFR 1.84 and MPEP § 608.01(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence Listing Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A Sequence Listing is required when the application discloses nucleotide or amino acid sequences as defined in 37 CFR 1.821(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Sequence Listing must be submitted in accordance with 37 CFR 1.821-1.825 and MPEP §§ 2421-2431. A Sequence Listing is required on paper if not submitted electronically on compact disc or as a text file via EFS-Web.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Examiner Form Paragraphs for Abstracts and Related Defects
rubrics_metrics.description: The MPEP provides form paragraphs (e.g., 6.12–6.17, 6.16.01) that examiners may use to notify applicants of missing abstracts, improperly placed abstracts, objections, or required corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs include examiner notes about pro se applicants, national stage exceptions, and specifics for what to indicate in brackets (e.g., informalities requiring correction). See the cited form paragraphs in MPEP § 608.01(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of the Specification
rubrics_metrics.description: For completeness of the specification, ensure all required sections, references to drawings, disclosure of best mode, and support for claim terms are present so that the specification provides adequate support for prosecution and establishment of disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See cross-references to MPEP §§ 608.01(p), 2161, 2162, 1302.01, 2111.01 and related guidance throughout the specification sections.
